To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mean HU‐shift and the noise‐level in the image have a significant influence on the dose recalculation.
the mean HU‐shifts in the fat and muscle regions are the most sensitive to dose deviations.

the dose recalculation for tomotherapy is sensitive to HU‐shifts in the water‐density region (fat, water, muscle) but not in the high and low density regions (bone and air) and that noise has no influence on the dose recalcuation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to use the tomotherapy MVCT‐images to monitor the treatment.
the effect of MVCT image parameters on dose recalculation for TomoTherapy.
the question of how the MVCT‐image quality affects the dose calculation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dose recalculation is robust to changes in mean HU and Gaussian noise levels up to 30%.
the MVCT image should have a HU‐shift of less than 30HU and a noise‐level of less than 20% to ensure dose recalculation within 2%.
the HU‐shifts in MVCT images can be used for a strict QA‐protocol for MVCT images, but the dose‐recalculation should be performed on the patient's own image.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a simple image‐quality QA protocol can be established for tomotherapy.
the MVCT‐image should be used to monitor the treatment, but not for dose recalculation.
the HU‐shifts are not a problem for the MVCT‐recalculation, but the noise level can be a problem, especially in regions with low densities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a strict QA protocol can be devised for the MVCT‐ beam using simple and easily accessible image parameters.

it is possible to devise a QA program based on simple parameters, which can be performed on a weekly or even monthly basis, instead of the current daily QA program, which requires service interventions.
the tomotherapy MVCT beam is sensitive to HU shifts and noise levels, and that a simple QA program can be devised to monitor the beam stability.
